# Lab 4.7: PIVOT, UNPIVOT & TABLESAMPLE

## What We Are Going to Do
Turn rows into columns with PIVOT, columns into rows with UNPIVOT, and explore a large table cheaply with TABLESAMPLE.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] PIVOT order status into columns.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab04.status_by_month AS
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE(created_at)) AS month, status
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders`
  WHERE created_at &gt;= '2025-01-01'
)
PIVOT (COUNT(*) FOR status IN ('Complete', 'Shipped', 'Returned', 'Cancelled'))
ORDER BY month;

SELECT * FROM lab04.status_by_month;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] UNPIVOT back to rows.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT month, status, orders
FROM lab04.status_by_month
UNPIVOT (orders FOR status IN (Complete, Shipped, Returned, Cancelled))
ORDER BY month, status;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Sample 1% of a big table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT COUNT(*) AS sampled_rows
FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.github_timeline` TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (1 PERCENT);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Compare **Bytes processed** with a full `COUNT(*)` on a selected column. Sampling reads about 1% of the storage blocks.

4. **[CLI] Check the cost difference with dry runs.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --dry_run 'SELECT repository_url FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.github_timeline`'
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --dry_run 'SELECT repository_url FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.github_timeline` TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (1 PERCENT)'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The dry run shows the full size for both, because sampling happens at run time. Run both and compare **bytes billed** in history.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| PIVOT | One column per status |
| UNPIVOT | Back to month/status/orders rows |
| TABLESAMPLE | Random blocks, not random rows |
| Bytes billed | About 1% of the full read |
